The purpose of this article is to present the Lean approach and the integration of its principles trough the supply chain, and show how this integrated approach can offer considerable performance improvement and provide a base for further contributions in this field.

articleTitle: Optimization of production system with environmental consideration: the effect of worker learning in a metallurgy factory
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Over the last few years, energy consumption and carbon emissions have been the subject of a great deal of attention, due to the ever-increasing climate change and diminishing of fossil energy resources. In this context, this article aims to minimize the maximum completion time (makespan) by taking into account environmental aspects in a production system. In particular, we consider a flow shop group scheduling problem with sequence-dependent setup times, learning effect related to the ability of each operator as well as machine speeds and the various carbon emissions associated with them, inspired by a real case study of the manufacture of forged connecting rods in a metallurgy factory. The objective is to determine both an optimal scheduling of the groups and the jobs within the groups in order to minimize the makespan by restricting the carbon emissions of the system. A mixed integer linear programming model is formulated, the computational results are also presented and discussed through the different scenarios.

articleTitle: The Balanced Scorecard, what impact on the performance of Supply Chain Management: Case of large business in Morocco
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The issue of Supply Chain Management performance is considered, within the framework of this research, through a management and piloting method, namely the prospective dashboard. For this, a theoretical analysis framework of our research problem was provided. Subsequently, a qualitative study was developed to test our research hypotheses. The results obtained confirm the idea that the impact of the balanced scorecard on the performance of supply chain management will be all the stronger as inter-organizational trust is reinforced between the various partners from the initial supplier to the final customer.

articleTitle: Port Performance Indicators: An Exploratory Study in the Moroccan Context
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to explore qualitatively the main determinants that measure and influence positively port performance in the Moroccan context. To achieve our objective, we mobilized the results of our systematic literature review previously carried out in an article and where we identified ten determinants of port performance measurement. Subsequently, these determinants were confronted qualitatively within 22 Moroccan port stakeholders. As a result, we were able to confirm the presence of the ten determinants noted previously and add three others, which were deemed critical and necessary according to our respondents. Finally, we were confronted with the prominence of port governance as the main key determinant of port performance. Thus, providing useful insights for further studies.

articleTitle: The potential use of Machine Learning in firms: The evidence of industrial enterprises
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The development of various types of technologies with the growth of the generation of huge amount of data from different sources (sensors, smartphones, social media, ...etc) have led industrial companies' management to new challenges to achieve at all levels, particularly in the supply chain. Taking useful insights from existed data could have a main role to provide a major gain in decision making within firms. However, it requires to contain different skills of the field of Artificial Intelligence especially the Machine Learning. In other side, industrial firms explain an enormous need to gain the support of Machine Learning to provide recommended plans for various Supply Chain's functions based on wireless collected data, especially for areas that need a high level of predictions and can generate through which a great reduce of firm's costs. In this context, this paper tries firstly to investigate the literature dealing with the use of Machine Learning under Supply Chain functions of companies through the word, and expose the case of industrial firms in Morocco with conclusions and perspectives in a second part.

articleTitle: Towards a more Hyperconnected, Smart, and Sustainable Urban Logistics: Development and Applications of Urban Logistics Platforms 4.0
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The main objective that has been proposed for this work has been the analysis of the aspects that can make urban logistics more efficient and sustainable, in terms of the application of logistics 4.0 and new logistics platforms. For its realization, the main restrictions that hinder the development of smarter and more sustainable cities were analysed, as well as the main metropolitan logistics problems. In the application of the new logistics platforms, the main aspects of its omni-modal, synchro-modal, intelligent and hyperconnected transformation were analysed, within the concept of sustainable global logistics. The result of all this will be the development of a new territorial planning and integration of commercial areas, logistics centres, routes, and corridors, in which the metropolitan areas will stand out as catalysts for their economic and logistical development.

articleTitle: Modeling the patient journey in a maternity unit of the UHC in Tunisia: an approach to overcrowding analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: We propose here to explore a process-centered management approach which is illustrated in particular in the case of care processes passing through the maternity service of the University Hospital Center of Sousse (UHC) Farhat Hached. This approach is intended to be followed by the patient in order to minimize his time in hospital and the costs of his care, while respecting the quality of care. Our goal in this article is to identify the stress situation activities and bottlenecks that contribute to overcrowding and the long queue. The biggest source of delay in patient flow is the wait time for health care demand. This modeling step was mainly a preparation for the simulation as well as the creation of a diagram enriched with information and summarizing the essentials of the functioning of the service to which we will be able to refer throughout our work. The development of this model was based on specific visits made to the Maternity Service (MS) of the Farhat Hached University Hospital Center (UHC) in Sousse. This modeling is necessary to represent the reality of the MS as faithfully as possible. It must be sufficiently detailed to produce an analysis making it possible to identify dysfunctions of the MS and also to identify situations of temptations.

articleTitle: Sustainable Supply Chain Management Practices and Firm Performance: Evidence from Small and Medium Enterprises of Pakistan
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to demonstrate if sustainable supply chain practices can lead to a positive corporate performance, in recent research internal efficiency has been emphasized over external effectiveness. This research explores two internal and two external management variables. Furthermore, the implications of Sustainable Supply Chain Management incorporation with regard to its related internal and external practices have not been explored in the literature with regards to developing countries and small and medium enterprises context. It is also noted that recognition of the economic benefits obtained from sustainability programs implemented can have managerial and practical implications but needs more evidences. Structural equation modelling approach is used for analysis whereby a theoretical model is adapted from previously published research. A purposive multi-industry approach to sampling was adopted to select environment friendly firms. After validity and reliability of data, the sample equation was analyzed using structural modelling for relationship effects. Firms can learn from the results to align their stance towards sustainable advancements as a competitive advantage.

articleTitle: Sustainable framework of Lean manufacturing implementation during supporting programs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: According to several research the implementation of lean brings important profits consequently progressively more Moroccan SMEs are oriented to pick this assistance from national supporting programs; however, the presence of issues prohibits the beneficiation and causes the drop of implemented practices. This article aims to investigate the status of some Moroccan small and medium enterprises SMEs which adopt the proposed program of Moroccan initiative of performances improvements INMAA by the implementation of lean manufacturing. The results show the level of each practice and the faced issues that could be avoid by the proposed framework of supporting programs for a sustainable lean manufacturing implementation in SMEs.

articleTitle: Contribution to the design of a logistics chain performance measurement system: case of a Moroccan SME group
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Our research problem is oriented towards the design of a system for measuring the logistics performance of a group of SMEs operating in several cities in Morocco (thanks to intervention research). Our general problem can then be stated: how to implement a logistics performance measurement system in the context of Moroccan SMEs. The objective of this research work is the design and implementation of a system for measuring the logistics performance of Moroccan SMEs using the GIMSI approach (Generalization, Information, Measurement, System, and Initiative). To achieve this objective, we have adopted a qualitative approach based on an abductive reasoning mode (back and forth between research work that addressed the question of the design of performance management indicators and our field of research (group of SMEs)).

articleTitle: Logistics pooling as a sustainable development service
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: With the development of logistics activities and the effects of globalization on international competition, innovative flow optimization concepts are emerging that not only focus on costs but also integrate corporate social and environmental responsibility as an essential challenge in a sustainable development approach. It is within this framework that we can add the logistic mutualization(pooling) based essentially on the collaboration between the different partners, that allows us to reach a global optimum. However, this culture is not yet anchored in MOROCCO. For this reason, our present article focuses on the demonstration of the impact of this concept on costs and the minimization of greenhouse gas emissions through a modern case study of application, and the analysis of the efforts of the Moroccan State to encourage companies to adopt this model.

articleTitle: Rail transport as a service for sustainable mobility Case: ONCF MOROCCO
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Transportation is considered as an important factor of pollution. It represents a quarter of CO2 emissions in the world, most of this emission is caused by road transport. On the other hand, according to the statistics of the International Energy Agency, rail transport is less polluting, it emits only 3% of greenhouse gases. In Morocco only 8% of the transport market share is occupied by this mode. In this article we will try to show the potential impact of increasing the market share of rail transport on the minimization of greenhouse gas emissions, as well as the achievements of the ONCF, the only operator in Morocco.

articleTitle: Application of Eco-driving among logistics service providers in Vietnam: Can the method of Delta International Co. Ltd., be diffused?
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Our paper analyzes the implementation of an eco-driving training for truck drivers in a Vietnamese logistics service provider, Delta International Ltd. Eco-driving, despite already well acknowledged ecological and economic benefits among developed countries, remains scarcely adopted by Vietnamese drivers. Since April 2018, while still concerned by excessive CO2 emission and logistics costs due to fuel consumption of its truck fleets, Delta has become a logistics pioneer by encouraging Delta's drivers to adopt eco-driving techniques into real conditions. By training Delta's drivers to eco-driving practices and by rewarding them extra income based on the value of saved fuel, Delta International Ltd has chosen an original path that inquires its possible diffusion among other Vietnamese 3PL. We adopt a qualitative approach based on interviews with Delta's CEO, Delta's drivers and about twenty Vietnamese 3PL to estimate whether Delta's eco-driving model may be adopted by other Vietnamese 3PL. We also illustrate the experiences, the highlights, and the drawbacks of Delta's eco-driving strategy.

articleTitle: Green scheduling of permutation flow shop with tool deterioration and constrained tool replacement: A case study from metalworking industry
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE 13th International Colloquium of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: Recently, there has been a growing scientific and political concern about global warming and its effects on the environment. Since the industrial sector is the number one world-wide contributor to this phenomenon with its huge discharge of Carbon Dioxide (CO2), researchers are looking for effective way to improve carbon efficiency in manufacturing plants by investigating scheduling strategies aiming at reducing the greenhouse effect of production processes. In this paper, we consider a permutation flowshop scheduling problem with constrained tool replacement activities where the tools needed for processing jobs are susceptible to deterioration and need to be replaced with new ones supplied from outside the system at prescheduled moments. The objectives of the scheduling problem are to simultaneously minimize the total carbon emission and the maximum completion time. A Non-Linear Mixed Integer Programming formulation for the problem is developed. This exact approach is demonstrated with a real-life case study of a turning process that is handled by a multi-spindle machine tool. To obtain approximate non-dominated solution sets in reasonable time, an enhanced Non Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) combined with a Simulated Annealing algorithm (SA) is adopted. Computational results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm to solve the problem.
